# The port contracts, as data

What any build’s ports must do, as cases a harness runs: the same cases Faro’s own tests run on its adapters (`src/ports/contracts/`). A team that copies Faro’s code passes them with its adapters; a rebuild passes them with its own ports, through a small shim.

## A contract file

Each `<port>.json` holds `port` (the name the shim is asked by), `about`, `ops` (each operation the shim answers, with its arguments and what it does), `given` (what a case starts from) and `cases`. A case is `{ "name", "given"?, "steps" }`: a sentence saying what any build must do, its own `given` when it doesn’t start from the contract’s, and its steps, each `{ "when": { "op", "args" }, "then" }`. A step with `pages` calls its operation again with the last answer’s `next` put in as `after` (in the argument at `pages.arg`), until `next` is null or `pages.max` calls; `pages.each` is checked on every answer, and `then` on `{ "pages", "rows" }`: how many calls were made, and every page’s rows in order. `pages.between`, when given, is an operation called once after the first page and before the second: something that happens while someone pages, such as a goal added.

What a `then` checks (every key given must hold; an empty `then` only asks that the operation doesn’t refuse):

- `select`: a path into the answer that the other keys look at: `total`, `rows[0].name`, `rows[].id` (every row’s id), `[].id` when the answer is a list. Inside `all` and `anyOf`, each path starts from the whole answer again.
- `equals`: equal as JSON: the same keys (a key left out and one holding nothing are the same), the same values, lists in the same order.
- `has`: at least this: an object’s keys as deep as given (others may be there too), a list’s items one for one.
- `includes`: a list holding each of these, anywhere in it.
- `excludes`: a list holding none of these.
- `length`: a list or text exactly this long.
- `maxLength`: a list or text no longer than this.
- `distinct`: a list with no item twice.
- `ordered`: `"text"`: A to Z in the language’s own order; `{ "rank": { … } }`: by each item’s rank, highest first, ties in any order (stale and at risk tie, so worst first is checked this way, not by a fixed list).
- `throws`: the operation refuses: the shim answers `{ "error": … }`, in any words.
- `absent`: nothing there: the key is left out, or null.
- `all`: every one of these holds.
- `anyOf`: at least one of these holds: where the contract accepts either of two answers (a near miss is optional).

## The shim

A command that answers one JSON request per line on its standard input with one JSON answer per line on its standard output, in order, and nothing else on standard output (write anything else to standard error). A request is `{ "port", "op", "args" }`; the answer is `{ "ok": <the answer> }`, or `{ "error": "<words>" }` when the operation refuses. Each case starts with `{ "port", "op": "given", "args": [<given>] }`: start that port afresh from it, and answer `{ "ok": null }`. An operation with no answer answers `{ "ok": null }`.

Name it in `drill.json` beside (or instead of) `run`, and the harness runs every contract here through it:

```
{ "stage": 1, "run": "node main.mjs", "shim": "node shim.mjs" }
{ "shim": "node shim.mjs", "contracts": ["search"] }      only these contracts, and no CSV files
node spec/rebuild/drill.mjs rebuild --contracts prefs      one contract while you work
```

It prints each contract’s count of cases that pass, then each failing case with what went wrong, and exits 0 only when every case passes (and every scored CSV file matches).

## The contracts

### [search](search.json)

The Search port: one search per kind of thing (goal, person, team, and any a module registers), answered a page at a time; what a list bar, a picker and Find ask. `given` is a workspace (`SearchSeed`: workspace.json’s records, with each person’s job title `role` and `leftAt`), searched as it stands at its `builtFor`. A row is `{ kind, id, name, detail, status?, key? }`; an answer `{ total, rows, next, near? }`.

- `given`: Start a fresh search over this workspace. Answers null.
- `kinds`: The kinds it answers, core first.
- `search`: (kind, { q, filters?, sort?, after?, size? }) One page of the things of this kind that match, in the kind’s order: `{ total, rows, next, near? }`. Refuses a kind nobody registered.
- `suggest`: (kind, viewerId, recents) Up to 6 rows offered before anything is typed: you first, then your team, then those chosen lately (`recents`: `[{ kind, id }]`).
- `byIds`: (kind, ids) The rows for things already chosen, in the words a search gives and the order asked, someone marked as left included; an id it can’t find is left out.

Its 10 cases:

1. answers the core kinds, and refuses a kind nobody registered
1. finds a goal by its key, however it is typed, and a key finds only its own goal
1. matches the words on the row: each word typed starts one of its words, ignoring case and accents
1. lists rows in two lines: a goal with its status and key, a person with their job and team, a team with its lead
1. takes a Goals link’s filters and sort, and orders goals worst first when unsorted
1. pages by key: every row once and none twice, with the total on every page
1. never gives a picker someone marked as left
1. suggests, before anything is typed, you first, then your team, then those chosen lately
1. gives the rows for things already chosen by id, in the words a search gives, someone marked as left included
1. may offer a near miss when nothing matches, and says nothing when nothing is near

### [prefs](prefs.json)

The Prefs port: a few small values per person and workspace that aren’t records (the things they opened lately, the Goals scope they used last). `given` is null: each case starts with nothing kept.

- `given`: Start with nothing kept. Answers null.
- `get`: (workspaceId, personId, key) The value kept under `key` for this person in this workspace; null when there is none.
- `set`: (workspaceId, personId, key, value) Keeps `value` (anything JSON can hold; null forgets it) for this person in this workspace only. Answers null.
- `reopen`: Open the same store again, as a new page load would: what was kept is still there. Answers null.

Its 3 cases:

1. reads a value back for that person in that workspace, and for nobody else
1. keeps a value when the store is opened again
1. forgets a value set to null, and a later value replaces an earlier one

### [goals](goals.json)

The query port’s goal calls (`Goals`): what Home, Goals and the AI tools read about goals, a page of summary rows at a time, each row what the stage 1 rules say about the goal now. `given` names the conformance workspace (`workspace.json`, beside this folder) as it stood at its `builtFor`, asked by `viewer` (for scopes): the shim makes a port over it. An ask is `{ query, scope?, after?, size? }`, where `query` is a Goals link’s query string (`status=off&sort=title`; the Goals screen’s filters and sort, [the Goals page](../../core/rules/goals-page.md)) and `scope` names a Goals scope, answered for the viewer. A row is the goal’s summary without its check-ins: `goal` (the record), `status`, `attention.flags` (each with its `kind`) and the rest.

- `given`: Start a fresh port over this workspace, for this viewer. Answers null.
- `goals`: (ask) One page of the goals the query matches: `{ rows, next, total, near? }`, at most 50 rows whatever `size` asks for, in the query’s sort, or worst first then by title with no sort. `next` is the key to ask the next page with (`after`), null on the last; `near` is the near miss a search found nothing for (find rule 5).
- `counts`: (ask without paging) `{ total, status, attention }` for the same filter: how many match, how many in each status, and how many need attention with the query’s own attention filter left off.
- `goal`: (id) One live goal’s summary with its check-ins (`checkIns`); null for a goal that isn’t live here.
- `add`: (goal) A goal is saved to the workspace by someone else, between two of your calls: later calls see it. Answers null.

Its 24 cases:

1. answers the Goals query (every goal) as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “status=off” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “status=off,risk” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “attention=1” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “attention=1&needs=stale” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “team=cicd” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “owner=rhea” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “level=north-star” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “kind=milestone” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “q=tunde” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “q=rolback” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “q=zzzz” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “quiet=2” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “feeds=ns-lead” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “sort=title” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “sort=last” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “sort=due.desc” as goals.csv says
1. answers the Goals query “status=on&sort=gap” as goals.csv says
1. gives each goal the status and flags the rules give it (status.csv and flags.csv, this week)
1. pages by key: every goal once and none twice, and a goal added between pages doesn’t move the next page
1. never gives more than a page, whatever size is asked for
1. gives a goal’s check-ins only through goal()
1. narrows to a scope by its name, for the person asking, and counts the same filter
1. lists with no sort worst first, then by title

**Not yet as data:** the goals store’s contract (`storeContract`) is still only in Faro’s code; it moves here when the store’s windowed load and history land.
